Interface LogFormatter.PostProcessor

All Known Implementing Classes:
LogFormatter.StandardPostProcessor
Enclosing interface:
LogFormatter
public static interface LogFormatter.PostProcessor
Rewrites the text a formatter has just written for an event, for example to prefix every line or to escape line breaks. Unlike a formatter, a post processor sees the finished text of the whole event, including message arguments and stack traces.

Post processors apply only to encoders backed by a formatter, such as the default encoder, the pattern encoder and LogEncoder.of(LogFormatter). Encoders that write bytes directly, such as the JSON encoders, ignore them. They are selected by name with the "logging.appender.{name}.encoder.postProcessors" property: 

logging.appender.console.encoder.postProcessors=crlf,journald

They run in the order listed, each on the text the previous one left, so the order changes the result. With crlf,journald a multi-line event becomes one line with one prefix. With journald,crlf every original line is prefixed and then the lines are joined.

A post processor changes only the text of the encoder it is configured on. The event is not changed, so other appenders, other encoders and anything else that reads the event see the original values.

Like formatters, post processors must be thread-safe. One instance processes every event of its encoder, possibly from several threads at once, each with its own StringBuilder.

The LogFormatter.StandardPostProcessors are registered under their lowercase names when the LogConfig is created. Others are added with register(ServiceRegistry, String, Provider). A name that is not registered fails when the encoder is provisioned, with an error listing the registered names.

  • Method Details

    • process

      void process(LogEvent event, StringBuilder output, int start)
      Rewrites the event's text in place. Only the text from start to the end of output belongs to this event; text before start must not be changed. output is the encoder's buffer, which the encoder sizes and trims, so a post processor that needs working space should use output itself, for example by appending the rewritten text and deleting the original, rather than a buffer of its own.
      Parameters:
      event - the event that was formatted.
      output - the output, whose text from start to its end is the event's text.
      start - index where the event's text begins.

    • decorate

      default LogFormatter decorate(LogFormatter formatter)
      Wraps a formatter so this post processor rewrites everything it writes.
      Parameters:
      formatter - formatter to wrap.
      Returns:
      formatter.

    • register

      static void register(ServiceRegistry registry, String name, LogFormatter.PostProcessor.Provider provider)
      Registers a post processor under a name so encoders can select it with "logging.appender.{name}.encoder.postProcessors", usually from a RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator. A name that is already registered, including the name of a LogFormatter.StandardPostProcessor, is not replaced.
      Parameters:
      registry - usually LogConfig.serviceRegistry().
      name - the name used in the property.
      provider - creates the post processor, given the encoder's name and config.
